bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Customer concentration (top 1 minus next 4 metric improving but still relevant); Commodity/semiconductor cost inflation; El Nino impact on monsoon (domestic 2W demand) and US hurricanes (genset demand); R&D execution risk in new segments (CV, Power Tools).

bull_bear.body: Confident and data-driven; Emphasized technology moat (sensorless) and regulatory tailwinds; Transparent on risks (surveyed investors); Conservative on specific forward-looking product revenue splits but aggressive on volume trends.

bull_bear.body: Sensorless technology eliminates physical sensors entirely (not just reduces count), solving reliability issues (water/dust ingress) in EVs and enabling ISG in wet-magneto engines where competitors fail; ISG+EFI integration creates a 'hard to argue against' economic proposition for OEMs despite potential single-source hesitation.

deepdive.thesis: SEDEMAC delivered a breakout FY26 with 61% revenue growth to INR 1,058 Cr, driven by regulatory-mandated ISG adoption in 2/3-wheelers and robust industrial genset demand. The investment case hinges on the proprietary sensorless control technology enabling cost-effective integration (ISG+EFI) and expansion into high-volume power tools and commercial vehicles, funding organic capex with >40% RoCE.

open.item: MF3 at Chakan, Pune is scheduled to commence operations in Q2 of FY 2026-27, more than doubling the Company's available production area.
Shipments are expected to start from MF3 (120,000 sq ft, ECUs) and MF4 (9,000 sq ft, electric motors), both in Chakan, during FY 2026-27.
Start of production of engine and exhaust gas after-treatment controllers and motor controllers for the Commercial Vehicles market is expected over FY 2026-27.
Company will focus on strengthening its digital backbone in FY 2026-27 to improve scalability and build redundancy against external cyber threats.

Company is operationalizing two new manufacturing facilities in Chakan, Pune — MF3 (primarily electronic controllers) and MF4 (electric machines/motors) — as part of a phase of rapid manufacturing expansion.
Company has acquired land in Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu (upcoming MF5) to cater to South India customers and diversify plant locations.
Company is actively working towards offering ECU products for the Commercial Vehicle market within the Mobility segment.
Company is actively working towards introduction of MCUs for the Power Tools market, having already secured a first business win with a small but established manufacturer for an SLC-based MCU.
Company sees an opportunity to reach a volume of more than 10 million motor controllers per year for the 2&3-wheeler market, driven by increasing ISG penetration and growing electrification.
Start of production of the SLC-based MCU for the Power Tools market (first business win already secured) is expected over the next four to five quarters.

Customer concentration (revenue from largest customer minus the sum of the next four) fell from 72% in FY24 to 68% in FY25 and further to 58% in FY26; management expects continued ISG penetration and growth in Commercial Vehicles/Power Tools to further lower this risk in the mid-term.

Company is moving into manufacturing electric machines/motors, starting with those for 2&3-wheeler ISG systems, and is engaging with customers on an integrated rare-earth-free motor with MCU for electric 2&3-wheelers and e-bicycles.

Electric motors integrated with gearboxes for ISG applications will be the first mechanically-intensive products from the Company's expanded electromechanical/mechatronic capability to enter production.

drhp.business: SEDEMAC designs and supplies critical-to-the-application, control-intensive Electronic Control Units (ECUs) to major OEMs in India, the US and Europe, acting as a Tier-1 automotive/industrial supplier. It operates across two segments — Mobility (ISG, EFI, combined ISG+EFI ECUs and motor control units for ICE and electric 2&3-wheelers) and Industrial (genset controllers and EFI ECUs for power generators) — and has shipped more than 12 million control-intensive ECUs to date.

risks.note: The Chairman's Key Risks section states that rapid market expansion of an innovative proposition relies on anchor early adopters and 'often results in a situation of customer concentration'. The company's own concentration measure — revenue from the biggest customer minus the sum of the next four customers — was 72% in FY 2023-24, 68% in FY 2024-25 and 58% in FY 2025-26. Management names Sensorless ISG penetration plus growth in Commercial Vehicles and Power Tools as the levers expected to lower this only in the mid-term, so a single OEM's model cycle or sourcing decision remains the dominant swing factor on revenue.
risks.risk: Customer concentration — TVS Motor Company is the single most significant customer, having adopted the SLC-based ISG proposition since 2018

risks.note: The AR states that because revenue has historically had a high dependence on supply of products for engine-powered 2&3-wheelers, a shift of the Indian 2&3-wheeler industry towards electrification poses a risk to the business. Management frames two primary questions: whether it has compelling propositions for electric 2&3-wheelers, and whether OEM thinking on vertical integration would reduce the size of its addressable market. Migration to date is early: products supplied to the electric 2&3-wheeler market rose from 0.3% of 2&3-wheeler revenue in FY 2023-24 to 1.7% in FY 2024-25 to 7.4% in FY 2025-26 — broadly only in line with the EV share of the Indian 2-wheeler market, i.e. tracking the shift rather than out-running it.
risks.risk: Electrification of the Indian 2&3-wheeler market, plus OEM vertical integration, against a revenue base historically dependent on engine-powered 2&3-wheelers

risks.note: Management states success has historically depended on introducing innovative technology that unlocks new markets (smart ignition for carburetted 2&3-wheeler engines, electronic governing in genset controllers, SLC motor control without position sensors), and that each new proposition must pass a defined sequence — technology proposition and proof of concept, commercial business win, initial introduction, early growth, broader market adoption, sustaining industry proposition. Each stage introduces distinct risks and 'any failure at any stage, whether due to technical, commercial, operational, or market-related factors, can limit our ability to open new markets and grow our business.' This is the structural counterpart to the concentration risk: the de-concentration plan itself depends on the pipeline converting.
risks.risk: Dependence on continued success in developing and commercialising substantial new technology propositions — failure at any stage of the innovation pipeline caps new-market entry

risks.note: In the FY 2026-27 Outlook, management names commodity price inflation due to geopolitical instability together with tightening semiconductor supply chains as a factor that could raise raw material costs and 'may create mild pressure on EBITDA margin in the near term'. Material cost is the company's dominant expense line, so semiconductor availability and pricing sit directly on the gross margin for an electronics control-unit business with limited near-term pricing offset disclosed.
risks.risk: Input-cost inflation and tightening semiconductor supply chains flagged as a near-term dampener on EBITDA margin

risks.note: The FY 2026-27 Outlook names as the second potential dampener that forecasts of a strong El Nino in CY2026 raise the possibility of a weaker Indian monsoon and a less active US hurricane season, which could negatively affect India's 2-wheeler market and the US home-standby generator market respectively. Both of the company's demand pools are therefore exposed to the same climate driver in the same year. Management characterises both as global factors affecting the industry at large and states it does not see either as a structural threat.
risks.risk: Weather-driven demand exposure in both principal end markets — a strong El Nino in CY2026 threatening the Indian monsoon and the US hurricane season simultaneously

risks.note: The growth that is reducing customer concentration is itself lodged in a small number of specific design wins: ISG adoption in two more of the top-4 Indian OEMs 'including on some key models' over FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, the EFI ECU adopted as default by the North American genset market leader in their key model in FY 2025-26, and an FY 2026-27 expectation of introduction on variants of three top-10 2-wheeler models across three of the top four OEMs. The electric-machine foray (rare-earth-free motor plus MCU) is described as an emerging mid-long-term opportunity whose contribution is contingent — 'if our electric machine foray works out well'. Slippage in any one model programme moves a disproportionate share of the growth.
risks.risk: New-market/new-product ramps concentrated in a narrow set of OEM model wins, including the North American genset default adoption

risks.note: The Corporate Governance Report records the Risk Management Committee as constituted on 13th October, 2025 under Regulation 21, with a mandate spanning financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability, information and cyber security risks, business continuity planning, risk tolerance and appetite levels, and a policy review cadence of at least once in two years. Cyber security is singled out repeatedly in the terms of reference (framework for identification, implementing and monitoring policies and processes). The framework is therefore newly stood up rather than seasoned: the equity shares listed on 11th March, 2026, and the Stakeholders Relationship Committee held no meeting at all in the stub period to 31st March, 2026, so there is not yet a track record of the risk apparatus operating through a full listed cycle.
risks.risk: First-year listed-company risk governance — the Risk Management Committee was constituted only on 13th October, 2025, months before the 11th March, 2026 listing
